correctness.rationale: For the normalized conic parametrization, the opposite chords give Pascal coefficients [−z, x(y+z−1)+z, −xyz]. Distinct vertices give distinct opposite-side intersection points, and the quadratic conic restriction has discriminant z²D with z nonzero. For distinct y,z outside {0,1}, the x-quadratic discriminant has character χ(y(y−1)z(z−1)); it is nonzero, and the linear cases y+z=1 have character sum zero and one root each. Removing x=0,z subtracts two sets of square values. The x=1 and x=y exclusions factor into the two stated products; their sums are both −2q+6+χ(−3), giving A_S−A_E=−3q²+20q−33−2χ(−3). For tangencies, the two deleted zero sets have q−4 members each; the resulting A_T is (q−4)(q−5). The nonsplit line orbit is transitive, since an affine F_q transformation can send any nonrational parameter in F_{q²} to another, carrying conjugates along. The other two orbits follow from transitivity on conic points and pairs. Dividing each normalized tally times |PGL₂| by its orbit size and by the free dihedral factor 12 gives the claimed per-line counts. In particular (6,6,48) at q=7 is the normalized tally, whereas (6,21,64) is the correct per-line tally. All three formulas are positive for permitted q≥7, and q=5 has only exterior lines hit. Direct independent censuses agreed at q=5,7,11.
residual_risks: The independent census is over prime fields only. The source records a separate finite F_25 check; the character-sum argument proves every extension degree in scope.
The title omits the q=5 exception; the mathematical Finding explicitly states it and limits surjectivity to q≥7.

evidence: The enumerative article treats fixed-line fibers and simultaneous prescribed-line constraints over the complex field. The degeneration paper treats collisions over a complex conic. The finite-field spectrum ranges over many characteristics, but fixes the sextuple and imposes genericity.

value.rationale: The rational fiber sizes of a classical map give more than an existence result: they distinguish the three line orbits, quantify the field-dependent discrepancy, and explain the first-size exception while proving all-line surjectivity in larger fields. The exact per-line count is useful for finite conic incidence calculations and is not a recomputation of the F_5 catalogue alone.
residual_risks: The result does not cover repeated vertices, characteristics 2 or 3, or simultaneous constraints on several Pascal lines.
